subject: Holistic GPU footprint & SLA sizing framework for VectorForge pilot
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@vectorforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-07-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: GPU sizing kickoff — VectorForge pilot

Elena —

Thanks for taking this on. To get our pre-sales sizing right for the pilot, can you share a short (bullet) traffic snapshot? The things we typically need to size Dedicated capacity are below — a CSV or a sample telemetry export is perfect:

- Typical request pattern: steady vs spiky, daily/weekly seasonality
- Peak QPS (and burst window width, e.g., 30s/5min) + expected duration of peaks
- Average request tokens (prompt) and average response tokens
- Typical session/conversation length (messages per session) and session affinity needs
- Concurrency targets (p99 connection concurrency if you have it)
- SLA/latency targets (p95/p99) and acceptable cold-start behavior
- Any multi-model routing (e.g., short-form vs long-form models) or fallback acceptance

If you can attach a small sample (one week) or paste a short table, we can produce a back-of-envelope GPU footprint and a suggested pilot topology (reserved pool, burst policy, prewarming). I attached a short template (columns) — feel free to drop your CSV.

Goal: have a sizing workshop next week and a draft mutual action plan with an initial committed pool + burst plan.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@vectorforge.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@vectorforge.com
Date: 2024-07-13T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GPU sizing kickoff — VectorForge pilot

Avery —

Appreciate the template. Attaching a small extract (vf_traffic_snapshot.csv) from our staging logs — it's anonymized. Quick highlights to save you time:

- Baseline (weekday): 8 QPS average, with 90th percentile bursts around 45 QPS for 2–3 minute windows during business hours; weekend baseline drops ~40%
- Peak observed: 120 QPS (rare), typically during marketing campaigns; peaks last 5–20 minutes
- Prompt lengths: median 120 tokens; Response lengths: median 240 tokens (we have a mix of short and long generative tasks)
- Session shape: conversational chat flows, average 6 messages per session; we keep session state for up to 30 minutes of inactivity
- Concurrency: application-level concurrency target is 60 concurrent sessions at 95th percentile during normal ops; during peak bursts app accepts graceful queuing up to 180 concurrent sessions
- SLA: p95 response < 250ms for short prompts, < 800ms acceptable for long-form responses; p99 we target < 1.5s and are flexible for pilot
- Models: we plan to serve a small ensemble: one 7B fast encoder for short replies and one 33B-ish optimized for long-form; willing to accept quantized variants for cost reasons

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call. What does your team need for the workshop?

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform, VectorForge
elena@vectorforge.com

Attachments: vf_traffic_snapshot.csv (10KB)

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Elena's snapshot. Quick takeaways and asks before the workshop:

- Traffic shape: sustained low baseline with frequent short peaks (45 QPS for 2–3m) and occasional marketing-driven surges (up to 120 QPS). Burst profile suggests we should recommend a small committed pool + a burstable reserve.
- Token economics: median prompt 120 / resp 240 — avg per-request tokens ~360. For initial cost estimate assume 0.35k tokens per request.
- Sessions: average 6 messages with session affinity for 30m — implies KV cache benefit if we pin to session workers.
- Model mix: 7B for short replies, 33B for long-form. Propose quantized 33B or an optimized 20–25B to save GPU memory unless VectorForge insists on FP16 33B.

Prelim sizing (very rough):
- Committed pool: 2x A100-80GB-equivalent instances to cover baseline concurrency and steady 45 QPS bursts with conservative batching (assuming 7B fast path + cached long-form KV hits).
- Burst reserve: autoscale to additional 4 GPUs for 15–30 minute windows when marketing campaigns trigger; fallback routing to smaller model if burst > cap to preserve latency.
- Warmup: prewarm KV cache for top 10% most active sessions for pilot window (saves ~15–25% token compute on average).

Workshop asks:
1) Elena to confirm the ratio of short:v long requests (we have samples but a simple split % helps)
2) Which latency tiers are non-negotiable (short prompt p95?)
3) Any compliance/retention constraints (session logs, KV caching allowed?)

I'll prepare two small artifacts before the call: 1) a one-page capacity diagram (GPU counts, instance classes, routing rules), 2) a runbook draft for pilot staging & failover. Attaching a lightweight checklist in the workshop agenda.
